snapshots.title: Button
Toggle Group
snapshots.content:
ToggleGroup accepts type single|multiple, controlled value/onChange, defaultValue, orientation horizontal|vertical, variant default|outline, size sm|default|lg and disabled. ToggleGroupItem requires value and exposes its selection through aria-checked and data-state. Documented SolidJS example: ```tsx import { createSignal } from "solid-js"; import { ToggleGroup, ToggleGroupItem } from "@/components/ui/toggle-group"; import { AlignLeft, AlignCenter, AlignRight, AlignJustify } from "lucide-solid"; export default function Example() { const [alignment, setAlignment] = createSignal("left"); return (
setAlignment(val || "left")} variant="outline" >

Selected Alignment: {alignment()}

); } ``` Source revision: ce75abc6a948d2d78b2b22d368c2997832d0909b. Preserve the source component classes and its matching theme/animation CSS. Preview compilation uses SolidJS 1.9.17 and babel-preset-solid 1.9.16. This is browser UI. Native Tauri v2 window, dialog and updater APIs require a desktop host and are not emulated in a browser preview.

snapshots.title: Timeline
snapshots.content:
Timeline accepts orientation vertical|horizontal, align left|right|alternate and size sm|default|lg. Compose TimelineItem, TimelineSeparator, TimelinePoint, TimelineConnector and TimelineContent; TimelineTitle, TimelineDescription and TimelineTime carry each event. TimelinePoint supports status variants; TimelineConnector supports dashed. Documented SolidJS example: ```tsx import { Timeline, TimelineItem, TimelineSeparator, TimelinePoint, TimelineConnector, TimelineContent, TimelineTitle, TimelineDescription, TimelineTime } from "@/components/ui/timeline"; import { Check, CreditCard, Package, Truck } from "lucide-solid"; export default function Example() { return ( {/* Step 1: Completed */}

snapshots.title: Introduction and Quick Start
snapshots.content: Nikala UI is a copy-paste component system for SolidJS and Tailwind CSS v4. The official Quick Start initializes Nikala UI in an existing SolidJS project with the CLI init command, then uses add button card input theme-manager to copy components into the workspace. Select a package-manager command on the official page. Component code is imported from local aliases such as @/components/ui/button, not from an invented aggregate npm component package. Keep the generated Tailwind v4 theme tokens and local cn helper. The preview examples use browser UI; Tauri v2 desktop integrations require their native host. See the official CLI Reference and Theming Guide linked from the docs for project-specific alias and theme configuration.
